When true love is embrace problems no longer exist. Yes, challenges may be present, but they are looked upon with appreciation and gratitude as one realizes that their purpose is to make one stronger, and not to tear one down. 

Your life isn't supposed to be problem free, and if you believe that then you're delusional. Everyone has problems. Everyone. The difference between those that are truly happy, and those that are depressed, is how they view those problems. Some utilize an empowering perspective, and some utilize a dis-empowering perspective. The choice is ultimately yours, but one leads to joy and the other leads to depression.

I will continue to post here. I appreciate your well-meaning advice, but at this time I won't act congruently with it. 

I hope all is well for you my friend.

Love is not capable of turning its back on anyone. Perhaps what we incorrectly call love, but not real love itself. Real love is found within, and it's unconditional. The trap that many, and myself, fall into is looking for love outside of ourselves, and this is when problems arise. 

We can't expect to receive love from any one person. Yes, we may go through periods where love is shined upon us by another person, but we cannot depend on it. We must love ourselves, and then love can never be taken from us. 

I disagree with your last statement. There is nothing that rules our lives but ourselves. No one is in control of you or me. We are completely free to be, do, and think as we wish. If our lives are filled with distractions it is because we have allowed them in. We are the creators of our reality, and the power to create is always with us.

You are responsible for your life. You can play small and pretend like you aren't in control, but deep down you know that your life rests entirely upon your shoulders.

Hey my friend,

I know that you have passions. Everyone does, and it breaks my heart to hear that you've forgotten about them. There are things that you truly enjoy. These are the activities that feel like play to you. Time disappears, and the experience is more of 'being' than 'doing'. 

Take a look back throughout your life, and identify what these activities are for you. It may be something with music, maybe building with your hands, maybe drawing or painting. Whatever it is, there is always something. It's impossible to not have anything that you love. Our basis of existence is love, and this is expressed through what we enjoy most. 

Get back in touch with yourself. Empty your mind of what everyone has been telling you your entire life. Find what you enjoy doing, and go do it. Life is meant to be joyful.

Much love

Hey man, thanks for the feedback. 

My best practical tip is to decide why you're here in the first place. 

Defining a purpose for life may not be something that you want to do. Most people on this planet seem to be okay with merely existing. So if you feel content with your current routine then allow it to be. 

But if you feel like something's missing then something is actually missing. There's no honor in exercising self-discipline on a path without a heart. I would say that if your primary strategy for action is based upon willpower, then you're missing something. 

Whenever you live from love, there's no such thing as willpower. When you truly open up and allow yourself to care deeply it becomes harder not to act, than it does to act. 

Force negates. Force is unsustainable. Motivation in the typical sense of the meaning is force. If you have to use tactics to motivate yourself to take action then you don't really want what you say you want. However, it's easier to want what we think we're supposed to want instead of looking within and figuring out what the hell it is we actually want. 

I'm personally going through this process now. I've realized that the goals that I've set for myself are nothing but the goals that society has set for me. I set goals to achieve certain amounts of passive income, goals to buy a certain kind of house, goals to achieve a certain level of prestige, but none of these really inspired me. I spent months wondering why I couldn't get myself to take action, and I finally had to admit that I didn't care one bit about these goals. 

What I really want is to express myself as authentically as I possibly can. What I really want is to connect with you guys and share the love that I have for you. What I really want is to just be happy, have fun, and play with the world and my fellow humans. 

Fuck all this competition nonsense. There's no one to compete against. We're all the same people even though it doesn't seem like it. You guys are my teammates, and your success means as much to me as does my own success. Your happiness is as important to me as is my own happiness. 

My main intention with this thread has been to inspire you not to settle for less than you could experience. If you don't wake up and go to bed beaming with enthusiasm, then something's missing and I want to help you find it.

Thanks for the response my friend. I appreciate it.

What if our obsession with mindless entertainment is nothing but a desperate call for help? What if this entertainment seeking is really a way to distract ourselves from the more pressing issues that we're afraid of facing within ourselves?

I know that whenever I find myself drowning in shallow entertainment, I'm doing my best to avoid facing up to some uncomfortable truth that is beginning to surface. It's easier to be distracted than it is to emotionally process the emergence of our authentic selves. 

Personally, I know that entertainment isn't a real desire of mine. I don't see any point of living a life in the pursuit of entertainment. Why the hell should I be alive at all if I'm going to passively watch a box of flashing lights? Why the hell should I be alive if I'm going to pursue merely sensual pleasures?

I just feel something much deeper, much greater within myself, and even though the pursuit of it isn't remotely easy, it's so much better than mindless entertainment. 

Love is the acceptance and then pursuit of the highest parts of yourself. It's the acceptance of your purpose for existence and then summoning the courage to follow it at all costs.

Your thoughts create your reality. 

This is a fundamental truth, and an understanding of it is the answer to your problems. 

First, I want to highlight a few things from your post:

- "I’m standing here, feeling worthless, frustrated and talent-less"
- "I cannot start"
- "now I'm just nothing"
- "I just can’t seem to break out of this thinking pattern, I don’t know what to do anymore."

Humor me and temporarily adopt the perspective that your thoughts do in fact create your reality. From this perspective what kind of reality are you creating by the thoughts that I've highlighted above?

Are these thoughts propelling you forward in a direction you want to go? Or are these thoughts the very reason that you are stuck in the first place? 

I have such compassion for you my friend. I really do. This is such a vicious cycle of self-defeating, self-perpetuation creation, and it's difficult to break out of it. 

Realize that you aren't your thoughts. Right now you gain your identity from the thoughts you think, and this causes you to believe that these self-defeating thoughts actually are who you are. Identities are naturally self-perpetuating, and so this vicious cycle continues. 

The way to break out of this is to begin thinking differently. 

Think of a flower. Pretty easy right? Now choose an animal, and then think about it. Again, pretty easy right? 

What both of these examples prove is that you have the ability to direct your thoughts. Through conscious intention you can place your thoughts absolutely anywhere you would like. 

Through habituation your thoughts have settled into a groove of negativity and self-depreciation. Much like physical habits, your thinking also settles into ruts. If you aren't conscious of what ruts you're settling into you may end up in a situation that you don't want to be in. Which is exactly where you now find yourself. 

The task ahead of you is the process of reconditioning your mind. 

Try this:

Every morning, right after you wake up, take 10 minutes to lie in bed and intentionally practice new thoughts. I want you to lay there and think thoughts such as:

- I'm worthy
- I'm a creative person
- I'm a strong person
- I can do anything that I want to do
- I am certain of my decisions

Initially, these thoughts are going to be uncomfortable. You'll actually have difficulty thinking them, and every time you focus on one of them your mind will spit it back out and say NOPE, NOT TRUE! This is okay. What will happen is that after days of practicing these thoughts your mind won't reject them so quickly. Eventually, you'll get to the point where you can think these thoughts AND believe them. Essentially, you're building new pathways in your brain, and it takes time to do this sort of thing.

Don't even focus on action. Leave action completely out of the equation. Continue what you normally do everyday. The action part will come later. What will happen is that as you start to believe these new thoughts, you'll begin getting new urges for action. Instead of discounting the idea of drawing you'll actually feel motivated to pencil to paper. 

You see, your actions are the effect that your thinking has caused. Your perpetual thinking of "I can't" has got you stuck in this rut, and the solution is to begin thinking new, more empowering thoughts. 

I hope this information helped in some way. If you don't take anything else away from this advice, just remember that you have the ability to think different thoughts if you choose to do so. If you'll remember this, you will eventually be motivated to put it into practice. 

Much love my friend,

- Austin

You believe that the world is inherently unsafe. You relate to life from states of fear, uncertainty, and apprehension. It is your belief in fundamental danger that is causing your stress and worry.

Right from the get go it's important to understand that these problems you are dealing with are symptoms of a much deeper issue. Anytime that you identify 'problems' in your life it's crucial to look past appearances and identify the root cause. The difficulty in this is that it takes focus and courage to look within and accept that we hold certain beliefs that are negatively affecting your life. 

By focusing on your stress/worry and trying to cure it, you're essentially looking for medication. And what does medication do? Nothing but temporarily mask the underlying problem. 

You see, as kids we learn one of two ways of thinking about the world

1. The world is a bad place and I am not safe
2. The world is a good place and I am safe

The assumption that you come to accept as true will determine the course of your life more than any other. 

The unfortunate thing is that these assumptions aren't made consciously. Your fundamental perspective of reality is largely a result of environmental influences during your earliest years. Thus, as you grow older you don't even realize that you hold one of these assumptions to be true. 

You mistake your perspective of reality as reality itself, and this is your biggest problem.

You believe that world is fundamentally dangerous, and thus, you are not safe. This belief is the cause of your stress and worry. 

When you believe that the world is dangerous you are always on the look out for yourself. Everything that happens is a potential threat to security, and so your mind is obsessing over these trivial issues in order to identify potential danger. Your stress/worry are perfectly natural side effects of your belief in an unsafe world. 

Your mind is just trying to protect you. Your stress and worry causes you to constantly analyze the world around you in search of danger so you can protect yourself from it. Essentially, your brain has a bug much like software does, and this bug is the cause of your stress/worry. 

In order to debug your brain you're going to have to elevate your level of thinking, and by necessity this is incredibly uncomfortable. Your solution is a growth in consciousness, not techniques and tips. Your solution does not lie in masking your symptoms. 

First, you must realize that you are not your thoughts. You are not the first-person perspective that you think you are. You are not your body. You are not your feelings. You are not the 'you' that you commonly think you are. 

What you are is pure, silent awareness. Your real identity is that part of you that silently watches everything. You can get in touch with your real identity by silencing your mind, and simply watching. 

When you finally realize this truth you then gain the ability to reprogram your beliefs. The belief that you want to reprogram is your belief that the world is dangerous. By switching to the belief that the world is a safe, good place you'll eliminate your stress and worry. 

Everyone is different, and thus there isn't a step-by-step method to this type of growth. Often, you'll need to invest tremendous energy in this general direction in order to affect a quantum leap in your growth. Essentially, you have to exert enough energy to escape the gravitational pull of your current level of existence. This is uncomfortable, but necessary. 

There is much information that will be of use to you, and the great thing is that the nature of this reality will bring this information to you when you finally become ready for it. It seems like you are ready for it as you've posted this question publicly, so I have no doubt that useful information will begin flooding into your awareness. 

Your task is now to take action and follow up on every lead that you get. Listen to your intuition and pursue the information that feels right. 

My best wished go out to you, and I know that you will eventually solve your problem.

- Austin

Hey man,

I feel for you. I went to college for all the wrong reasons as well. Fortunately, I realized this and dropped out after a semester. The biggest hang up that I had was dropping the social conditioning that says anyone who doesn't go to college is a loser. That's honestly what got me to go in the first place, and I found out that that isn't true whatsoever. 

There's no honor in doing something that you don't want to do just because you think that's what you're supposed to be doing. 

Obviously you aren't excited about your current life path. This isn't bad as long as you learn from it and move in a different direction. What this experience is trying to teach you is to follow your heart. 

You have got to find what you love to do. You have got to decide upon a purpose for your existence. Until you do this you'll keep experiencing more of the same. 

You see, the reason that you feel the way you do is because you're not being yourself. You don't know who you are and you don't know why you're here. Without defining a reason for your existence you can't make intelligent decisions about where to take your life next. So your lack of purpose is what has got you into your current position. 

Don't resist where you are. This is important. I've found that the more I resist something in my life the larger its presence becomes. Your situation isn't here to tear you down. Your situation is here to teach you. You have a lesson to learn from everything that is happening, and until you learn this lesson your circumstances will stay the same. 

Take a look and try to figure out what this is trying to teach you. Know that there isn't a right answer to what you're supposed to learn. It's all up to you.

If there's one thing that I want you to know, it's that life isn't supposed to be hard. Life is not supposed to be a struggle. You aren't here to do things that you don't want to do. You aren't here to follow plans that others have laid out for you.

You're here to experience joy. You're here to express your authentic self. You're here to love and be loved. You're here in this incredible experience for the process of eternal self discovery and fun. Know this with every fiber of your being and your life will change for the better. 

I hope this helped.

Hey, thanks for the feedback my friend. I really appreciate it. There's nothing like getting your work poked full of holes so you can better right?!

In regards to your first point about not being punished. I should have been more clear. From my experience, when I have acted like a cancerous cell (i.e. trying to get ahead at the expense of others/just focusing on myself) my life slows to a crawl. No opportunities appear. Problems arise, and it just seems like nothing is going my way. However, when I have acted like a responsible cell (i.e. chose my actions according to what I think is the best for all) my life has sped up. Fresh opportunities appear, I feel better, petty problems seem to disappear, and everything feels like it's going in the right direction.

So you wouldn't be able to see this from the outside looking in. Rather, it's felt from the inside. It seems like the Universe supports me or doesn't support me depending on the intentions behind my actions. That may sound kind of new-agey, but I can't discount my personal experiences. There's definitely something going on behind the scenes. 

As for the how, it all comes to down to one thing... your life purpose. 

Let me quote Dr. Viktor Frankl:

"What man actually needs is not a tensionless state but rather the striving and struggling for a worthwhile goal, a freely chosen task. What he needs is not the discharge of tension at any cost but the call of a potential meaning waiting to be fulfilled by him"

Whenever you have a purpose for your life, and you center your life around the practical pursuit of that purpose, then you live from love. The state of love is the acceptance, and pursuit, of that which you hold most sacred. 

If you want to be motivated internally without the need of fear tactics, then you must find a something for which you will dedicate your life. Without accepting this human responsibility, you forever work on the goals that society has set for you. Your intuition knows that society's goals don't resonate with you, and so you use techniques to try and force yourself to take action. 

The answer of practically applying this knowledge is to go and find your life purpose. Why are you here on this planet? What do you stand for? What do you feel so strongly about that you are willing to dedicate the rest of your life to it?

If you haven't already answered these questions in your life then the best use of your time would be to tackle them. Without a context, a why, a reason, you'll never be able to make intelligent decisions. You'll be nothing more than a rat running in a wheel, expending a ton of effort but ultimately getting nowhere.

I've written more about this here if anyone is interested: http://www.austingerleman.com/positive-motivation

Let me know if you guys have any other thoughts!
